description: A state-variable filter from a 2020 DAFx paper by Werner and McClellan, with saturating nonlinearities added inside the loop, and an attenuverter beside every control

params.text: Sets the filter frequency, 20Hz at the left to 20000Hz at the right
Scales the frequency control voltage and inverts it below the middle; at full clockwise ten volts there moves the knob across its whole range
Sets the resonant feedback around the filter, 0 to 0.95, taking it towards self-oscillation as it is turned up
Scales the feedback control voltage and inverts it below the middle; at full clockwise ten volts there moves the knob across its whole range
Sets the damping of the passband, 0.25 to 1.25; the lower the setting the more the filter rings
Scales the damping control voltage and inverts it below the middle; at full clockwise ten volts there moves the knob across its whole range
Sets how hard the three saturating elements inside the filter loop are driven, from a tenth to ten, with makeup gain applied after them
Scales the drive control voltage and inverts it below the middle; at full clockwise ten volts there moves the knob across its whole range

inputs.text: Shifts the filter frequency, scaled by the attenuverter beside it and added to the knob
Shifts the feedback, scaled by the attenuverter beside it and added to the knob
Shifts the damping, scaled by the attenuverter beside it and added to the knob
Shifts the drive, scaled by the attenuverter beside it and added to the knob

notes: each control voltage jack does nothing until the small knob beside it is moved off its centre, because the voltage is multiplied by that attenuverter before it reaches the control.
the filter runs at twice the sample rate when the module is added; the oversampling menu changes that.
menu: Oversampling: 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x — sets how many times the internal sample rate is raised before the nonlinearity is computed; higher settings reduce aliasing and cost more CPU
Publication — opens the 2020 DAFx paper this filter comes from in a web browser

inputs.1:

unpatched it reads 0V, so the knob alone; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob; the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 1V.
